content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository pulp-platform_common_cells_pr192, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# Width mismatch error in assign statement with VCS strict compile
In the below assignment, the RHS being a genvar is 32-bits wide, while the LHS which is parameterized and need not be always of 32-bits wide. Thus the compiler throws a width mismatch error.
https://github.com/pulp-platform/common_cells/blob/0989ff73d0315922791bf42137c0ce0cbb4a76ca/src/onehot_to_bin.sv#L26
Can the code be modified to be generic enough with the assignment like this,
``assign tmp_i = i[BIN_WIDTH-1:0];``

<analysis>
The core of the error is the assignment on line 26: “assign tmp_i = i;” attempts to drive a BIN_WIDTH-bit vector (tmp_i) with the full 32-bit genvar index i. Under strict compile this width mismatch is disallowed. To fix it, every usage of i in this context must be explicitly truncated or cast to BIN_WIDTH bits. Additionally, we should review:

1. The calculation of BIN_WIDTH itself (line 16) to ensure it matches expectations and doesn’t inadvertently collapse to zero or negative values.
2. The declaration of tmp_i (line 25) which defines the sink width.
3. The assign statement (line 26) which must be modified to “assign tmp_i = i[BIN_WIDTH-1:0];”.
4. The subsequent use in tmp_mask (line 27) to confirm that j is always within bounds of the truncated tmp_i.
